style: Organised, hard-working and physically committed under Tony Popovic. Defensively disciplined with set-piece threat from tall defenders, transitioning quickly through energetic midfield runners and pacey wide players.
recent_form: Qualified via the AFC pathway and arrive with a settled squad mixing experienced World Cup campaigners and emerging talent. Solid but unspectacular form heading into the tournament.

key_players.name: Maty Ryan
key_players.note: Vastly experienced number one and team leader; reliable shot-stopper and organiser.

key_players.name: Jackson Irvine
key_players.note: Combative engine in midfield, set to feature at his third World Cup.

key_players.name: Jordan Bos
key_players.note: Attacking full-back who pushes into the box while keeping defensive duties.

key_players.name: Harry Souttar
key_players.note: Towering defender and major aerial threat at both ends from set pieces.

key_players.name: Alessandro Circati
key_players.note: Composed young centre-back anchoring the back line.

key_players.name: Nestory Irankunda
key_players.note: Pacey, direct attacker offering flair and a goal threat off the flank.

historical_news: Veterans Aziz Behich, Milos Degenek and Jackson Irvine set to appear at their third World Cup.
50-cap forward Mitch Duke retired internationally before the squad departed pre-camp.
Socceroos drawn in Group D alongside the USA.
Squad blends experienced campaigners with a new generation including Irankunda, Bos and Circati.
Eight players departed before the squad left its Sarasota pre-camp.

media_sentiment.label: neutral
media_sentiment.summary: Measured expectations; respected for organisation and resilience but viewed as needing the right breaks against stronger group rivals to advance.
